podcast.body: "Video Killed the Radio Star" by The Buggles was the inaugural music video aired on MTV when the channel launched in 1981. This iconic broadcast ushered in a new era of music consumption and presentation, profoundly impacting the industry. "Pretty much everybody knows what the first video on MTV was when they debuted in 1981. It was video killed, the radio star for the Buggles."

podcast.body: This single scraped the US Top 40 at the end of 1979. It became considerably more famous two years later when it was the first music video played on MTV's launch day, August 1, 1981, despite being nearly two years old at the time. "The duo of Trevor Horn and Jeff Downs, whose 1979 single Video Kill the Radio Star, scraped the US Top 40 at the end of that year, and would become considerably more famous two years later."

podcast.body: This song holds the historical distinction of being the very first music video ever played on MTV, just after midnight on August 1, 1981. Its title proved ironically prophetic for the music industry's future. "It was the bugles and video killed the radio star."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was notably played as MTV, after 44 years and 5 months since its launch on August 1, 1981, shut down the last of its global music video-only channels at 6 am GMT on December 31, 2025. The song marked both the beginning and the end of MTV's pure music video era. "And it ended just as it began, with the bugles and video killed the radio star."

podcast.body: This song, released two years before MTV's launch, was ironically chosen as the very first music video ever shown on the channel at one minute after midnight on August 1st, 1981. Although it had only reached number 40 in the US upon its initial release, its prominent placement on MTV catapulted music onto a new trajectory, emphasizing the visual medium. "Video Killebba Radio Star was the first video shown on MTV."
